k014: One container watches servers, network gear, NAS, hypervisors, cloud services and websites. Useful alert rules are on from the start, and they stay quiet until something needs you.
k016: Then open http://localhost:8080 and create the first account. Image for amd64 and arm64: ghcr.io/laupernoe/dumbmonit.
k021: DumbMonit is before 1.0 (@@VERSION@@ is the current release). It runs every day on its author's network, but the HTTP API and the database schema can still change between minor versions; the changelog says how to upgrade. Some integrations have only met test instances. Try it, and tell us what breaks.
k056: Useful rules are on right after install. The work goes into sending fewer, better messages.
k058: Declare a switch as the parent of what sits behind it. When it goes down you get one notification, not thirty; the others read “Suppressed by parent”.
k060: A NAS whose array degrades sends one message per cycle, not one per disk. Reminders, escalation, acknowledgement, snooze, per-monitor ignore and clearing resolved history are all built in. A bell on each monitor counts its active alerts.
k062: Anomaly detection with no threshold to tune: 168 buckets, one per hour of the week. It stays silent for its first 14 days and only shows what it would have fired.
k064: “This filesystem will be full within four days” is listed as a forecast, apart from what is broken right now.
k065: Maintenance, silences and a notification policy
k066: One-off or weekly windows, hysteresis, flap hold, quiet hours, batching and an hourly cap, so a bad night does not become two hundred pushes.
k070: Each one has a Test button and a setup page in the documentation.
k093: An agent for what does not speak SNMP
k094: A small binary that pushes CPU, memory, disks, network, services and uptime to the server, plus temperatures, fans, SMART and ZFS pools where the machine exposes them. It calls the server, never the other way round: no port to open on the machine.
k095: A PowerShell script is served at /install.ps1 for Windows. The agent is also an image, ghcr.io/laupernoe/dumbmonit-agent.
k098: x86_64 and aarch64, systemd or OpenRC. Docker containers and OS health (updates, pending reboot, failed units).
k100: x86_64, installed as a Windows service. SMART through smartctl.
k103: launchd, Apple silicon and Intel; binaries attached to each release. Not yet run on real hardware.
k105: rc.d, x86_64, ZFS pools. Not yet run on real hardware.
k107: In relay mode an agent runs the server's probes (SNMP, Proxmox, HTTP…) from its own network — a second site, a client's network or a VPS behind NAT — with nothing inbound: no VPN, no port to open. Monitor a remote site
k108: Status pages for the people you serve
k109: Public pages at /s/<name>: groups of services with 90 days of history, uptime, incident and maintenance notices, email subscribers with double opt-in, RSS, README badges and a compact embed. A page can also be private, behind a password or single sign-on.
k110: Only the labels you choose leave the server. Monitor names, addresses and types never appear on the page, in a badge or in an email.
k113: A full-screen board for a room monitor: the verdict and the clock, the fleet figures, the health strip, open alerts and who is on call. Readable from across the room.
k115: Every supported monitor gets a 0–100 score and an A–F grade from the vendor’s own best-practice checks, PingCastle-style: category, severity, evidence, remediation, and a worst-first Security page.
k117: Admin, operator and viewer roles, TOTP and passkeys, an audit log, single sign-on over OpenID Connect or SAML, SCIM provisioning, and sign-in with LDAP or Active Directory. Account creation is off by default.
k118: Plays well with what you run
k119: /metrics, /federate and a Prometheus-compatible endpoint let an existing Grafana read DumbMonit's data.
k121: Every route behind /api/openapi.json (OpenAPI 3.1): scoped tokens (dmt_…, read or write) that can expire, be restricted to a network, and are rate-limited. API reference
k123: 27 tools for ChatGPT, VS Code or Cursor: read status, monitors, alerts, metrics and agents; a write token can also silence, acknowledge, add a monitor or restart a container. Secrets never come back. Connect an assistant
k125: Read the state, acknowledge an alert, start a maintenance window. Installable on the home screen, deliberately without an offline mode: it never shows yesterday's state.
k153: MIT, dependencies included: CI fails on any dependency that is not under an OSI-approved licence. No feature is held back for a paid edition, because there is none. DumbMonit is 100% free and will stay free.
k154: This site has no analytics, no cookies and no third-party requests.
k162: A monitor that reads wrong, an alert that woke you for nothing, a page that confused you: each report makes the next release better. Requests for a new kind of monitor are welcome too.
k165: DumbMonit · MIT licence · free, with no paid edition.
k170: the UI fills in the token for you

hl1_p: A single container with one volume and no extra capability. Open the page, create an account, add a monitor: graphs and alerts follow.
hl2_p: Useful rules are on from the start. Dependencies, grouping and learned baselines turn thirty messages into one.
hl3_p: Switches, firewalls, hypervisors, NAS, websites, databases and self-hosted apps, each read the way its vendor intends.
hl4_p: Public or private pages for your users and clients, with history, incidents and subscribers.
home_dev_p: Pick a family to see what is watched, the alert rules that come with it and what to prepare on the device.
home_cta_p: Three commands, or look at the live demo first.
f_lede: Alerting, agents, teams, status pages and the rest, in one container. What each kind of monitor reports is on the Monitors pages.
f_rep_p: Drag-and-drop dashboards, ten templates that fill themselves with your devices, a metrics explorer, monthly SLA reports as PDF or CSV, and a short scheduled email with availability and incidents.
f_topo_p: One picture of the whole infrastructure, drawn from what DumbMonit already knows: dependencies, relays, hypervisor guests and LLDP neighbours. Nothing to type in by hand.

f_lang_p: English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Portugal and Brazil), Russian and Simplified Chinese: the interface, this site and the documentation. Some translations are still partial.

in_lede: One container, three steps. Add the agent to your servers afterwards.
in_s1_p: Make a folder and fetch the file. It already drops every capability and mounts the file system read-only.
in_s2_p: Docker pulls the image and starts DumbMonit together with its time-series database.
in_s3_p: Open the page and create the administrator. Then add a monitor: the form says what to prepare on it.
in_req_1: Docker Engine with the Compose plugin.
in_req_2: An amd64 or arm64 machine (arm64 images come with the stable releases).
in_req_3: Port 8080 free, or another port of your choice.
in_req_4: Network access to the devices you monitor. Devices never need to reach the server; agents do, on TCP 8443.

co_lede: Everything is open: read the documentation, follow the code, report a problem or lend a hand.
co_docs_p: Guides, one page per monitor type, alert rules and the API reference, in nine languages on Read the Docs.
co_gh_p: MIT on GitHub: the code, the issues, the roadmap and the releases.
co_contrib_p: Add a monitor type, fix a bug, improve a page: the contributing guide explains how to start.
co_sec_p: How to report a vulnerability privately, and what the project does to stay safe.
co_tr_p: Translations are made by pull request, for the interface, the documentation and this site.
co_rel_p: Each release is tagged on GitHub, with its changelog.

fam_servers_blurb: Linux, Windows, macOS and FreeBSD machines through the agent, server hardware through its management controller, UPS units and Active Directory.
fam_network_blurb: Switches, routers, access points and VPNs: any SNMP device, MikroTik, UniFi, Tailscale and OpenVPN.
fam_cloud_blurb: Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Azure, AWS, Cloudflare, Hetzner, OVHcloud and Infomaniak: service health, licences, secrets about to expire, tunnels, servers and alarms.
fam_firewalls_blurb: OPNsense, pfSense, FortiGate and Sophos: gateways, tunnels, interfaces, high availability and licences.
fam_hypervisors_blurb: Proxmox, vSphere, XCP-ng, Nutanix and Kubernetes: hosts, guests, storage and cluster health.
fam_storage_blurb: Synology, TrueNAS, Unraid, Proxmox Backup Server and Veeam: disks, pools, and the age of the last good backup.
fam_checks_blurb: Web pages and APIs, ports, DNS, ping, TLS certificates, time servers, domain expiry, heartbeats and website changes.
fam_proxies_blurb: Traefik, Caddy, Nginx, Apache and Nginx Proxy Manager: backends, certificates and error rates.
fam_apps_blurb: Nextcloud, Immich, Paperless-ngx, Jellyfin, Plex, Home Assistant, GitLab and Forgejo.
fam_mail_blurb: Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, CrowdSec, and the mail servers and gateways: SMTP, MDaemon, SecurityGateway and Proxmox Mail Gateway. Blocklist monitors for a mail server or an IP range.
fam_data_blurb: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, RabbitMQ, MQTT, and the VictoriaMetrics, Loki and Graylog servers.
d_roadmap: What is planned for DumbMonit, in the order we intend to ship it, and what has already been delivered.
rm_lede: What comes next, in the order we plan to ship it, and what is already out. Plans can change: this page is updated with every release.
rm_discuss: Got an idea or a missing integration? Open a GitHub discussion.
hl5_p: Roles, per-folder rights, on-call and escalation. MSP mode keeps each client's sites, alerts and reports apart.
hl6_p: Every route in OpenAPI, scoped tokens, configuration as YAML, a CLI, a Terraform provider and an MCP server.
hl_h: Everything in one place, nothing to assemble
au_h: From a rack at home to the networks of your clients
au1_p: Proxmox, a NAS, a firewall, a few self-hosted apps. Add each one by its address and get graphs and alerts without writing a single query.
au2_t: An IT team of one to ten
au2_p: Active Directory, Microsoft 365, Windows and Linux servers, switches and backups. Roles, on-call and SLA reports, with no per-device pricing.
dg_h: Simple to run, simple to reason about
dg_p: One process supervises everything. Probes go out, agents call in, and every alert passes through one engine.
dg1_cap: One Rust binary with the interface built in. It starts VictoriaMetrics for metrics and keeps its configuration in SQLite: one volume to back up.
dg2_note: The connection is opened from the remote site, outbound only: no VPN, no inbound port.
dg2_cap: Agents and relays authenticate with their own certificate (mTLS, TLS 1.3) on the agent port, TCP 8443 by default.
dg3_s1s: a check fails or a value crosses a rule
dg3_s3s: what sits behind a down parent is suppressed
dg3_cap: A switch goes down: you get one notification for the switch, not one for each device behind it.
dg4_cap: Each client's sites, monitors, alerts and SLA reports stay apart, and accounts can be limited to one client.
f_team_p: What a small IT team or an MSP needs, without an extra product.
f_team1_p: One instance for several clients: each has its own sites, folders, alerts, dashboards and SLA reports.
f_team2_p: On-call schedules, cover swaps and multi-step escalation per person. Teams and permissions per folder.
f_team3_p: A ready-made kit installs the Windows agent on your domain servers, with the server address and port already filled in.
sup_p: DumbMonit is free and has no company behind it. If it saves you time, a donation pays for the test hardware and for the time it takes.
sup_home: DumbMonit is free and has no company behind it. Donations keep it that way.
sup_other: Bug reports, translations and device profiles help just as much.
au3_p: One instance, several clients. A relay agent per site, outbound only, and each client's alerts, reports and status pages kept apart.
cm2_p: Code, issues, roadmap and releases are on GitHub. Questions, ideas and device requests go to the discussions.
